newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end barely changed.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed little changed on Tuesday, with the metal's strong performance on the London Metal Exchange (LME) failing to attract investor interest.
"Prices have come down quite far. But individual speculators showed little appetite," said one trader. "With the trade volume so low, it is not really functioning as a market."
The TOCOM benchmark April 1998 contract was up 0.2 yen at 188.3 per kg after finishing at its contract low on Monday.
Other contracts were unchanged to 0.6 yen higher.
Estimated trade volume was 2,444 lots, little changed from 2,923 lots on Monday.
In the Tokyo precious metal futures market, which is enjoying bouyant trade, platinum futures climbed to hit their daily price limit on heavy short-covering.

In London overnight, three-month aluminium crawled up $6.00 to finish at $1,603 a tonne, above a key $1,600, helped by a warning by a U.S. industry analyst of a larger-than-expected supply deficit this year.
